        Five-star combo guard Adan Diggs committed to Arizona on CBS Sports HQ on Monday evening. The No. 6 overall player in the 2027 recruiting cycle by 247Sports marks the first member of the Wildcats' upcoming recruiting class.The Goodyear, Ariz., product committed to the Wildcats over Arkansas, Kentucky and USC. Diggs is the second-highest-ranked player from the 2027 recruiting cycle to pledge his college commitment. Last month, DeMarcus Henry — the No. 4 overall player in the class — committed to North Carolina. 
Other players from the 2027 recruiting class who recently committed include five-star center Lewis Uvwo (Providence), five-star guard Reese Alston (LSU), five-star forward Jordan Page (UConn) and four-star forward Asa Montgomery (Duke).Diggs is just the latest five-star that coach Tommy Lloyd has landed since arriving at Arizona in 2021, joining Caleb Holt (2026), Koa Peat (2025) and Brayden Burries (2025). 247Sports Director of Scouting Adam Finklestein says that Arizona is getting "one of the more naturally gifted two-way prospects in the national class."
"Physically, he has solid size for a combo-guard, good length (6-foot-7 wingspan), and an emerging power body. He's a good, not great, vertical athlete, who is better when he can elevate off two, and also a fluid mover. He's a very talented defender, both on and off the ball. He has some versatility, but can also impact the game around the rim. He's athletic and competitive on the glass (6.1 per game in EYBL) and capable of being the weakside low-man and even challenging plays at the rim."Arizona finished with the second-best recruiting class in 2025 and ranked No. 13 last cycle (2026) in the 247Sports rankings. With a commitment from Diggs, Arizona is on track to finish with one of the top classes in the 2027 recruiting cycle.

        Arkansas State has fired Butch Jones amidst his sixth season with the program, according to 247Sports. There's a chance that Jones could coach the last two games of the season, according to ESPN, but no decision has been made at this time.Entering November, Arkansas State was 4-4 with what appeared to be a manageable schedule ahead. Then, the Red Wolves dropped two winnable games to UL-Monroe and Coastal Carolina. That was the final straw for Jones, whose teams have gotten progressively worse over the last few seasons.Arkansas State hired Jones in 2021, and the team steadily improved in each of his first four seasons on the job — reaching bowl eligibility three times over that span. The Red Wolves' performance under Jones peaked with an eight-win season in 2024, but it has dipped in each subsequent year. Jones exits Jonesboro with an overall record of 30-43.
Jones began his coaching career as an offensive assistant and worked his way up the ladder at Central Michigan until he took over the program in 2007. After three successful seasons and two conference titles with the Chippewas, Jones made the jump to Cincinnati, where he won a pair of Big East championships.In 2013, Jones got an opportunity to coach at a major program when Tennessee hired him. He posted back-to-back nine-win seasons with the Vols in 2015 and 2016, but the team cratered in 2017, which led to his firing.
Jones then spent three seasons working as an offensive analyst for Nick Saban at Alabama before landing at Arkansas State. In 17 years as a coach, Jones has compiled an overall record of 114-97.

title: SEC abides by court order in RJ Luis eligibility saga: LSU free to add ex-St. John's star - CBS Sports
description: Luis is cleared to play -- without the threat of eventual punishment from the SEC -- after the league acquiesced
body:
Luis is cleared to play -- without the threat of eventual punishment from the SEC -- after the league acquiesced on Monday
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 16, 2026
                            
                    at
    6:52 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            3 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        It's the saga that refuses to die.The SEC on Monday was forced to stand down — for now, at least — in its fight to not allow LSU to roster former St. John's star RJ Luis. The soon-to-be 24-year-old has not played college basketball since March of 2025 but has used the legal system in Louisiana to circumvent both NCAA and SEC rules that state he is ineligible to play college basketball for the 2026-27 season.A preliminary injunction issued last Friday by a local judge -- Will Jorden of East Baton Rouge Parish -- was the necessary legal workaround that's enabling Luis to bypass the SEC's rule prohibiting former college athletes from leaving school, going pro, signing a contract and returning to compete in the conference.The SEC's rule was formally ratified in late summer amid a major controversy over LSU football's attempt to add two former Ole Miss players who were seeking to return to the conference after failing to make NFL rosters. In that case, the SEC stood firm and won.Here, a different outcome in favor of the Tigers. That preliminary injunction from Friday led to additional clarity on Monday from the SEC, which put out the following statement that was obtained by CBS Sports: "The SEC will abide by the terms of the preliminary injunction while it remains in place and will not impose penalties or fines on LSU if it places Mr. Luis on its men's basketball roster."
Whether the case returns to the courtroom during this season remains unknown. But an SEC source emphasized that although the league is adhering to the recent court order, it has no intention of giving up its fight on this front or similar ones.So, then, it would seem Luis is soon to suit up for No. 25 LSU, which just jumped into Monday's refreshed AP Top 25 after the Bayou Bengals upset 14th-ranked Gonzaga in Spokane, Washington, on Saturday. As of this story's initial publishing, LSU and its coach, Will Wade, have yet to comment on Luis' status. 
On an Oct. 13 Zoom call with a handful of media members, Wade said the following: "We're going to follow all the SEC protocols with him. I think it's been pretty clear what the SEC protocols are on all that. He didn't travel with us to McNeese, and he hasn't been rostered."But according to one of Luis' lawyers, he's gearing up for a quick return to the college ranks. "The SEC has confirmed in writing that it will abide by the court's order and will not penalize LSU for placing RJ on its roster," attorney Elliot Abrams told CBS Sports. "RJ has great respect for the SEC and its member institutions, and we are all grateful to the conference and to the Louisiana courts for working through this in an orderly legal process where everyone was heard. RJ is healthy, ready and looking forward to joining his teammates."
For the past week-plus, Luis had not been practicing with the team, per one source, but given all of the time, energy and legal rigmarole tied to Luis' fight over the past four months, it stands to reason Luis will join the roster -- and in the process potentially arm Wade's program with one of the 15-20 best rosters in college basketball. The Luis story picked up significant momentum on Aug. 24, when the initial temporary restraining order was handed down in Luis' favor -- and against the NCAA. Luis' legal team took the position that the SEC's rules are largely incorporated into the structure of the NCAA's bylaws. And though the SEC did make notable amendments to its eligibility rules in the summer, it did so months after Luis had started the process of trying to play for LSU. Thus, a Baton Rouge judge sided, in essence, with the local program and against the SEC's interests. In other words, Luis got through the gate before it was closed under the SEC's recently enacted policy. 
The latest plot twist in the story also lands amid a contentious federal lawsuit between LSU and the SEC that is ongoing in Alabama. That case was catalyzed by the aforementioned issue of LSU football trying to bring aboard players (tight end Dae'Quan Wright and defensive tackle Zxavian Harris) who spent the spring and summer trying to make NFL rosters. How that case is affected, if at all, by Luis' legal evasions in the coming months is unclear. Should Luis be added in the coming hours to the Tigers' roster, he'll join the likes of fifth-year player Donovan Dent, fifth-year player Skyy Clark and fifth-year player Austin Nunez as LSU players who needed a favorable court ruling to get on the basketball court this season.

title: Sean Payton disputes Jim Harbaugh's 'loophole' claim after Broncos-Chargers trade falls apart - CBS Sports

body:
The Broncos coach rejected Harbaugh's criticism of the process that derailed Denver's trade for Chargers linebacker Daiyan Henley
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 16, 2026
                            
                    at
    2:05 pm ET

        At the trade deadline last Tuesday, a rare inter-division deal was agreed to between the Los Angeles Chargers and Denver Broncos. The Broncos agreed to send the Chargers a fourth-round pick and a future fifth-round pick in exchange for linebacker Daiyan Henley, but the deal fell apart.The trade was nixed after Denver reportedly found an issue with Henley's knee during his physical. ESPN reported that the Broncos then approached the Chargers and attempted to renegotiate the compensation. Denver still wanted to acquire the linebacker, but just not at the price George Paton and Sean Payton initially agreed to.Chargers coach Jim Harbaugh told reporters last Thursday that the Broncos backing out of the deal sets a bad precedent, and that this is a "loophole" the NFL needs to investigate."That's why it's a loophole, and teams should not have the ability to do that," Harbaugh said. "It's a medical grade. It's a pass/fail for a medical trade. They told us they weren't going to pass him if there was a fourth and a fifth, which was agreed upon. They would not pass him for that. They would pass him for a fourth and a 'fill in the blank.' I don't know what to call that, but that's what it is."The Broncos were on a bye in Week 10, so we had to wait until Monday to hear their side of the story. Payton was indeed asked about the trade falling through, but didn't offer many details. 
"I'm not going to get into the specifics. He's prospect we thought of — and still do — very highly of. It just didn't work out," Payton said, via The Athletic. "I'll leave it at that."What did Payton think about Harbaugh's comments regarding a "loophole?"  "Listen, I thought I saw it all," he said, via Mile High Sports. "There's no loophole. It's just part of the trade process, every step of the way." 
Whatever the Broncos found in Henley's knee hasn't affected him yet. He hasn't missed a game due to injury in each of the last two seasons. In eight games played this season, Henley has recorded 51 tackles, half a sack, two passes defensed and an interception. The Broncos and Chargers will see each other again in the regular-season finale when Week 18 rolls around.

description: The former Wolfpack legend has returned to his alma mater to lead NC State into the 24-team CFP era in 2027
body:
The former Wolfpack legend has returned to his alma mater to lead NC State into the 24-team CFP era in 2027

        The voice of Philip Rivers trailed off as NC State athletic director Boo Corrigan helped him finish a final question about family to end Monday's introductory press conference. For the former quarterback and Wolfpack legend, coming home to Raleigh, North Carolina, was a calculated decision and quite emotional for Rivers."I've got a lot still to give and there ain't no better place or any place that I'd really want to give than right here at NC State," Rivers said, fighting back tears after detailing his return as football coach.Rivers comes back to his alma mater after spending the last six seasons as coach at St. Michael Catholic in Fairhope, Alabama. His son, 2027 NC State four-star quarterback commit Gunner Rivers, stars at the school and will be joining his father with the Wolfpack.Before a lengthy NFL career, Rivers was a four-year starter at NC State from 2000 to 2003, completing 63.6% of his passes for 13,484 yards, 95 touchdowns and 34 interceptions in his time playing for the late Chuck Amato, who died last month at 86 and was beloved at the program.
Rivers mentioned Amato in his message to the Wolfpack faithful and was direct on his plan to turn around NC State in the ACC next season and beyond."I don't have the manual, and I don't have the book, or the past years in college or the NFL to say, here we go, this is what we about to put together," Rivers said. "But I have it right here (pointing to his head) and here (pointing to his heart) and I've seen it right here. We're going to flood the (football ops) building with coaches and players that love football, that have high character and are committed to a relentless pursuit of victory."Rivers, who interviewed for the Buffalo Bills' coaching vacancy earlier this year, said he could already feel the energy returning at NC State and wants to coach with the same passion, conviction and discipline that he experienced as a player with the Wolfpack under Amato.
"I have this saying: the win-loss record goes to the quarterback and the head football coach and (I've experienced both)," Rivers said. "I probably got too much credit when we won and probably got too much blame when we lost. It's going to be about a great staff, a great locker room and a great group of people all in this thing together."I took great pride in responsibility in that was how it was looked at. I never learned the 'I' part of it. It's our team, it's our football program, it's our university. And that's the way we'll communicate and operate in the building."Corrigan said he had a conversation with Rivers the day after Dave Doeren was fired as coach last month, meeting the former quarterback with several of NC State's dignitaries and former NFL coach Bill Cowher in Fairhope, Alabama.
"Sitting around (Rivers') dining room table, I think it became abundantly clear that his passion for leadership and this university ... I remember coming back (to Raleigh) and telling my boss we have our guy," Corrigan said.NC State never reached the College Football Playoff under Doeren but was competitive in the ACC for much of his tenure. Doeren secured three top-25 finishes in 14 seasons and qualified for 11 bowl games (with four postseason wins).As college football moves into the 24-team playoff era next season, Rivers said Monday he knows he'll be judged on his initial win total and how competitive the Wolfpack look from the start.

Shifting target shares and changing workloads reveal which Fantasy players are gaining value and which are losing trust

        There were five players who scored at least 40 Fantasy points in Week 10 prior to Monday night, 12 with at least 31 points and 31 with at least 20 points. That's impressive with four teams on bye (Chicago, Denver, Philadelphia and Tampa Bay), and we love high-scoring weeks.  Two players who did well that we've had questions about recently were Nico Collins and Tony Pollard, and they are winners coming out of Week 10. And two players we wish were on this list but failed were Chris Olave and Sam LaPorta. Unfortunately, those players fall into the loser category.I'm not giving up on Olave or LaPorta yet, but I'm excited about the outlooks for Collins and Pollard moving forward. Let's find out why below.Week 10 Fantasy WinnersTitans RB Tony Pollard
Tony Pollard was playing well prior to his bye in Week 9 with consecutive games of at least 28.7 PPR points against Cleveland and Cincinnati. While that was awesome, he did that with Tyjae Spears (knee) out, and Spears returned for Week 10 against Jacksonville. The Jaguars matchup wasn't easy, and while Pollard was still a recommended start, I had some concerns. Pollard ended up with nine carries for 33 yards and eight catches for 66 yards and a touchdown on nine targets for 23.9 PPR points. He now heads into a dream matchup at Dallas in Week 11, and the Cowboys (his former team) are No. 1 in most Fantasy points allowed to opposing running backs. Pollard still faces Jacksonville again in Week 12 and Detroit in Week 14. Still, otherwise he has a fantastic remaining schedule (Washington in Week 13, Indianapolis in Week 15, Las Vegas in Week 16 and Pittsburgh in Week 17). He should be considered a top-15 Fantasy running back for the rest of the season.Texans WR Nico Collins
I was worried about Nico Collins prior to Week 10 at Cleveland. Not to the point of benching him, but his production was troubling. He scored 10.9 PPR points or less in three of his past four games prior to facing the Browns, including one touchdown. During that stretch, the Texans traded for Marvin Harrison Jr., got Tank Dell back from injury and started getting quality production from the combination of Jaylin Noel and Xavier Hutchinson. But in Week 10, Collins looked like himself again with nine catches for 94 yards and a touchdown on 16 targets for 24.4 PPR points. The targets and receptions were a season-high, and we hope that continues for the rest of the year. It's still a crowded receiving corps in Houston, but Collins remains the lead singer. Ideally, C.J. Stroud continues to pepper Collins with targets, and you see how great the results are for his Fantasy production when that happens. We just need it to be more consistent.
Week 10 Fantasy LosersSaints WR Chris Olave
Chris Olave remains a must-start Fantasy option, but the emergence of Jordyn Tyson could be an issue. Just go back to last season and look at Olave's production with and without Rashid Shaheed. In nine games in 2025 with Shaheed before he was traded to Seattle, Olave only averaged 14.1 PPR points. Without Shaheed, Olave was a monster at 20.2 PPR points per game in seven outings. This season, Olave averaged 17.8 PPR points in the first seven games while Tyson was out with a hamstring injury. In two games with Tyson, Olave is averaging just 11.4 PPR points. His production is obviously going to rise, but what happened against Carolina in Week 10 should raise a small red flag. Olave had three catches for 30 yards on four targets while Tyson had 11 catches for 80 yards on 13 targets. That was just his second game in the NFL, and he's only going to improve. How much will he take away from Olave moving forward? We'll have to see. But this development is enough to downgrade Olave slightly in the rankings for the rest of the year.Lions TE Sam LaPorta
Sam LaPorta went into Detroit's bye in Week 6 looking like a superstar Fantasy tight end. He came out of the bye looking like someone we should drop. In his past four games, LaPorta has scored 7.2 PPR points or less in each outing with no touchdowns, and he's averaging just 4.8 PPR points over that span. Now, two of those games were against the Packers and Vikings, who were the top two teams in fewest Fantasy points allowed to opposing tight ends prior to Week 10. But against the Dolphins and Patriots in the past two games, LaPorta has combined for five catches for 48 yards on nine targets. Amon-Ra St. Brown and Jamhyr Gibbs are the top options for the Lions, and Jameson Williams appears to be third in the pecking order. I'm not replacing LaPorta in my lineup yet unless there's clearly a better option on the waiver wire or via trade, if your deadline hasn't passed yet. We need to see something productive soon. We don't want LaPorta to be a liability going into the Fantasy playoffs.
For a deeper dive into the full game-by-game breakdown and additional start/sit advice, check out the full episode on the Week 10 Winners & Losers Fantasy Football Recap.

title: Ravens vs. Chargers prediction: Can L.A. get its first win on 'MNF' against the injury-plagued Ravens? - CBS Sports

body:
Plus, how to watch, odds, a preview and a prediction for the Monday night matchup

        In the Week 10 edition of "Monday Night Football," the Baltimore Ravens play host to the Los Angeles Chargers. Baltimore is coming off a disastrous Thursday night loss to the Jacksonville Jaguars, during which the offense looked inept with third-string quarterback Joe Fagnano under center while nursing an injury. The Ravens will now turn to the recently acquired Jacoby Brissett in hopes that he can reinvigorate the attack in the absence of both Lamar Jackson and Tyler Huntley. Los Angeles is in the midst of an epic disaster of a season, having started the year 0-8 and looking horrific on both sides of the ball. The Chargers are once again beset by a cavalcade of injuries, but that is no excuse for just how poorly they have played. They're the only winless team in the league at the moment, so they'll be looking for their first victory of the season.Will the Ravens bounce back, or will the Chargers finally get on the board? We'll find out soon enough. Before we break down the matchup, here's a look at how you can watch the game.Where to watch Ravens vs. Chargers liveDate: Monday, Nov. 16 | Time: 8:15 p.m. ETLocation: M&T Bank Stadium (Baltimore)TV: ESPN/ABC | Streaming: Fubo (try for free)Follow: CBS Sports AppOdds: Ravens -4.5, O/U 38.5 via DraftKings Sportsbook When the Chargers have the ballThe Chargers are 26th in the NFL in total yards and 32nd (a.k.a., last) in points. They average a mere 4.7 yards per play, which is 29th in the league, and they have scored points on only 27.4% of their drives while turning it over a league-worst 18.9% of the time. They lead the NFL in pre-snap penalties per game. They don't do anything well, and they often put themselves behind the eight ball with inexcusable mistakes. 
Justin Herbert looks like a broken quarterback, completing just 61.3% of his passes at an average of 6.8 yards per attempt, with six touchdown passes against a league-worst 11 interceptions. His receiver corps has been brutal all season, dropping passes and seemingly miscommunicating with him on routes left and right. He once again won't have Ladd McConkey on Monday evening, either, which will leave the uninspiring trio of Quentin Johnston, Tre Harris and KeAndre Lambert-Smith as his top perimeter options.Los Angeles has been entirely unable to run the ball, with Omarion Hampton, Keaton Mitchell and Kimani Vidal combining for 709 yards on 184 carries -- an average of 3.8 yards per tote. The offensive line has given them no room to run whatsoever, clearing the way for only 0.90 yards before contact per carry, according to Tru Media. The backs themselves have a slightly below-average avoided tackle rate, but they still check in considerably below average in yards after contact per carry.Other than all that, though, things are going really well!That said, the Ravens do provide the Chargers with an opportunity to at least move the ball. Baltimore is 25th in the league in scoring defense and 21st in yards allowed per play. The Ravens have shown themselves to be beatable mostly through the air, as they've allowed only 3.6 yards per carry this season. Herbert doesn't have his top receiving option available in this game, but if the offensive line can actually provide him with adequate time to throw (not a guarantee with this group, obviously), then perhaps he can throw the ball to the guys wearing his color shirts rather than the opposing team for a change.
When the Ravens have the ballIt's hard to know what to expect from Baltimore's offense given that the Ravens are now on their fourth starting quarterback. This time around, it is the one who has yet to play with his new team and arrived in town just a week and a half ago. We know that Brissett has completed 63.3% of his passes for only 5.6 yards per attempt this season, with 10 touchdowns against seven interceptions. We also know that he was benched in favor of Gardner Minshew before being traded from Arizona to Baltimore. He's competent and can keep the offense moving at times, but he doesn't offer much in terms of ceiling.We also know that Brissett likes to hyper-target his top options in the passing game. We saw that in Arizona with Trey McBride and Michael Wilson, but we also saw it in other stops, like when he honed in on Amari Cooper during his year as the starter with the Cleveland Browns. The Ravens already focus the majority of their passing game on wide receiver Zay Flowers, and it wouldn't be surprising if Brissett peppered him with targets here. 
Flowers was having a monster season with Lamar Jackson and even Tyler Huntley under center, but he did nothing the last two weeks with Joe Fagnano in the lineup, essentially. He should get back to producing at a decent level here, provided that offensive coordinator Declan Doyle moves him around the formation rather than parking him in the slot, where the Chargers have been better in coverage than they have been on the outside. Still, the Ravens will likely look to center the offense on Derrick Henry, so that Brissett doesn't have to do a ton of heavy lifting. Henry hasn't been as efficient this season (3.9 yards per carry) as he was during his first two years with the Ravens (5.6 per carry), presumably in part because he hasn't had Jackson to draw defensive attention away from his runs up the middle. Henry does still have a 53.7% rushing success rate, but he hasn't broken the types of long runs we've been used to seeing from him because the wider rushing lanes are not available with defenses crowding the box. He's run into an eight-man box on 30.9% of his carries, according to Tru Media, the third-highest rate among the 26 players with at least 100 rushing attempts so far this season.
The Chargers have actually been half-way decent against the run this year, allowing 4.1 yards per carry to opposing running backs, but they've been hit for explosives at an above-average rate. If they don't get Henry on the ground quickly, he could hit a crease and take it a long way. If that starts happening, it'll open things up for Brissett to work the play-action game, which could lead to big plays for the likes of Flowers, Ja'Kobi Lane and perhaps even Mark Andrews.PredictionI don't feel good at all about predicting the Chargers to actually keep a game close, but that's what I'm going to do here. I'm not going as far as predicting that they'll get their first win, but I think they can hang in the game against Jacoby Brissett in his first start with Baltimore. The Ravens' offense should be better than it was with Joe Fagnano under center, but I'm not sure it will fully hit the ground running right away. LA's offense is pretty broken, but the Ravens haven't exactly been great defensively (25th in scoring defense), so the Chargers might be able to put at least some points on the board. Prediction: Ravens 24, Chargers 20

body:
With no Power Four title game spots clinched, Week 12 could reshape conference races, CFP positioning and the Group of Six picture
        
                                                
                        
                        
    
                                            
                    
                    
                                            
        
    Nov 16, 2026
                            
                    at
    4:21 pm ET
                        
                •
            
            6 min read
            
        
    

            
    
        No team within the Power Four has locked in a conference championship game appearance entering Week 12 of the college football season -- and there's nothing better to describe what's been a wild few months of parity.Eight spots, four major standalone championship games and two weeks to sort it all out before we close the book on conference title weekend thanks to next year's arrival of the 24-team College Football Playoff. So much for a quiet sendoff.UCLA and Utah are the only unbeatens left on the board, each approaching top-4 seeds in the bracket by winning out. Sifting through the Power Four and various Group of Six conference races, we're updating scenarios on what you need to watch for on Saturday. Using a title-game simulator, we determined conference championship paths and various outcomes down the stretch.Paths narrow within the SECGeorgia can clinch a spot in the SEC Championship Game with a win Saturday night at South Carolina. As of Monday, the Bulldogs are 16.5-point favorites in that matchup, and the availability of Gamecocks starting quarterback LaNorris Sellers remains unclear after he missed his team's Week 11 loss at Arkansas.
Assuming the Bulldogs win that, here are all the scenarios for who they would play in Atlanta next month.If Alabama and Tennessee win out and finish tied for second, the Vols advance due to their head-to-head win over the Crimson Tide last month.If Alabama and Texas win out and finish tied for second, the Longhorns advance due to their perfect (4-0) record against common league opponents. Texas beat Tennessee, Mississippi State, LSU and would have beaten Texas A&M in this scenario. Alabama lost to Tennessee, but beat the others.If Alabama, Tennessee and Texas all win out and finish 7-2 in conference play, the three-way tiebreaker comes down to conference opponents' winning percentage. Since there's more than a half-dozen matchups left in SEC play, it may get very complicated. Alabama plays Auburn, Tennessee meets LSU and Vanderbilt, and Texas takes on Arkansas and Texas A&M.If Texas and Tennessee win out and finish tied for second, the Longhorns advance due to their head-to-head win over the Vols earlier this season.We're projecting the SEC to be a four-bid league in the CFP, with Georgia, Alabama, Texas and Tennessee getting in the final bracket.
        
            
                Bowl projections: Slotting all 47 games after Week 11 snuffs out CFP hopes for several contenders
                
                    Brad Crawford                
            
                            
    
                
                    
    
ACC scenarios are quite clearMiami didn't clinch a berth in its league title game after Louisville's win over North Carolina on Saturday night, but the Hurricanes can do so this weekend with a win over Virginia Tech. In fact, simply splitting its final two games with the Hokies and Boston College would be enough.
Given that advantage, here's who Miami would play in Charlotte next month with an auto-CFP berth on the line.If Wake Forest wins out against Georgia Tech and Duke, the Demon Deacons will get their rematch.If Louisville wins out and Wake Forest splits its final two games ending in a two-way tie, the Demon Deacons still grab the berth due to a head-to-head win over the Cardinals earlier this season.If Louisville wins out and Wake Forest loses to Georgia Tech and Duke, the Cardinals will play Miami in the final since they would be in sole possession of second place.If Duke wins out and there's a four-way tie for second at 6-3 with Louisville, SMU and Wake Forest, the Blue Devils are expected to advance due to the ACC's tiebreaker policy involving the SportsSource Rating Score. Duke would hold a head-to-head win over Wake Forest (in this scenario) and likely be the highest-ranked team left on the board within the ACC behind Miami.We're projecting the ACC to be a two-bid league in the CFP, with Miami and Wake Forest getting in the final bracket.Five teams alive in Big TenIn the Big Ten, UCLA and Indiana control their destiny. Behind those two is a three-team gridlock of teams with two conference losses -- Oregon, Ohio State and Iowa. Here are some -- but not all -- of the scenarios that could unfold over the next two weeks.
UCLA clinches a Big Ten Championship appearance with one win over its next two games (Michigan and USC).Indiana clinches a Big Ten Championship appearance by winning out against Washington and Purdue.If Ohio State and Indiana win out and UCLA loses to Michigan and USC, the Buckeyes play Indiana in the Big Ten Championship.If Ohio State and Oregon win out, Indiana loses to Washington and UCLA loses to Michigan and USC, the Buckeyes and Ducks will play in the Big Ten Championship. Ohio State has a head-to-head win over the Hoosiers, while Oregon holds wins over Michigan and USC in the event the Ducks are tied with UCLA with two conference losses.If Ohio State wins out, UCLA beats Michigan but loses to USC, and Washington beats Indiana and Oregon, the Buckeyes play the Bruins in the Big Ten Championship.If Iowa wins out, UCLA wins out, Nebraska beats Ohio State, Indiana loses twice, and Oregon loses to Washington, the Hawkeyes reach the Big Ten Championship by finishing in sole possession of second place at 7-2 overall in the conference.We're projecting the Big Ten to be a two-bid league in the CFP, with UCLA and Indiana getting in the final bracket.Utah and who else in the Big 12?Two teams are essentially vying for one spot in the Big 12 -- Texas Tech (9-1, 6-1) and BYU (8-2, 5-2) behind unbeaten Utah. While the Utes haven't clinched an appearance yet, we're going to assume Utah is one of the two teams playing next month for a right to win its way into the CFP as a top-4 seed. According to the Big 12, seven teams remain in contention, but wins by Utah and Texas Tech (coupled with a BYU loss to Kansas) this week send the Utes and Red Raiders to the title game.BYU holds a current tiebreaker over Texas Tech because the Cougars went 4-0 against common opponents Arizona, Arizona State, Baylor and TCU. The Red Raiders play Baylor and TCU to finish it out, and one loss would tie them with BYU for second and put the Cougars in Arlington.Like Utah, Texas Tech controls its destiny. Wins over Baylor and TCU the next two weeks put Joey McGuire's squad in its second straight Big 12 title game.Even if Utah loses its final two Big 12 games to TCU and West Virginia, the Utes hold a crucial tiebreaker with BYU since the Utes beat the Cougars head-to-head.We're projecting the Big 12 to be a two-bid league in the CFP, with Utah and Texas Tech getting in the final bracket. BYU would unfortunately hold the "first team out" designation in our latest predictions.
The Group of Six situationBoise State, the only Group of Six team that's currently ranked by the CFP committee, clinched a berth in the Pac-12 Championship Game at home with its 46-41 win over Oregon State. Liberty (Conference USA) and Louisiana Tech (Sun Belt) have also clinched appearances in their respective league title contests.According to the Pac-12, here are the updated scenarios for determining who plays Boise State in the conference championship:San Diego State would clinch the No. 2 spot with a win over Boise State.Texas State needs a win over Washington State and a San Diego State loss to Boise State to reach the final. The Aztecs hold the head-to-head advantage over the Bobcats.Oregon State needs a win over Utah State, a Boise State win over San Diego State, a Washington State win over Texas State, and a Colorado State win over Fresno State to get there. The Pac-12 states, "The Beavers would then need to win the three-team tiebreaker with SDSU and Texas State by winning Step 5 of a multi-team tiebreaker with a higher SportSource Team Rating score than both San Diego State and Texas State following the games on Nov. 21. The SportSource rankings are used by the CFP committee to help evaluate teams."We're projecting the Group of Six to have one bid in the CFP this season after New Mexico's loss to UNLV over the weekend ending any threat -- albeit small -- of producing a second entry.
